raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies an assembled, rearrangeable organizer and includes a checking step. Its 11-minute combined median exceeds the target; five partition complaints indicate a completeness concern without establishing the verified defect rate, and seven of ten observed customers succeeded unaided. Preassembly may expose insertion problems before dispatch, but that benefit is unmeasured. D2-O6 is a concrete limiting observation: both workers approached the time target on repeated simple layouts, so assembly itself is not established as the dominant bottleneck. Mixed-batch delays could reflect switching, layout complexity, or both. No proposed change is yet shown to meet all pilot targets.

openings.claim: Order-specific component staging and checking before insertion may reduce selection errors and mixed-batch delay while retaining full assembly.
openings.delta: Replace shared-bin selection during assembly with a temporary, order-labeled staging area containing the required partitions and selected exterior color.
openings.prediction: Within comparable layouts, staging reduces selection/checking time and discrepancies more than insertion time; benefits should be larger around layout changes if switching contributes.
openings.probe: Use existing parts and reusable spare-board staging areas in balanced current-versus-staged trials across both workers and layout types. Time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, including staging preparation and resets. Independently count components. Record layout transitions; reject apparent gains caused by simpler orders or shifted work.
assumptions: Trials fit available working time and the fixed delivery date.
Reusable staging fits the initial budget without increasing per-order materials beyond 0.40.
Product geometry, assortment capacity, partition removability and accepted selections remain intact.

openings.claim: An order-specific diagram locating the short partition may improve unaided setup because the current three-layout diagram leaves placement ambiguous.
openings.delta: Test informational ambiguity independently of workshop completeness and physical insertion difficulty.
openings.prediction: With verified complete kits, an explicit diagram reduces wrong placement and requests for location help; unchanged insertion retries would indicate a separate fit problem.
openings.probe: Assign the ten participants to five current-diagram and five order-specific-diagram first-use trials, balancing layouts. Record correct unaided arrangement within ten minutes, help requests, wrong-slot choices and insertion retries. Treat results as exploratory; verify printing cost and production time before pilot use.
assumptions: Replacement diagrams fit both cost limits and the delivery schedule.
No physical product or ordered arrangement changes are required.
Placement ambiguity is a hypothesis; overlapping widths do not exclude other mechanical causes.

raw.assessment: Neither alternative is validated. Preserve footprint, assortment, reversibility, ordered counts/colors, both cost caps and delivery date. Mixed-batch delays and insertion retries do not establish causes. Share at most 15 samples and ten participants across probes; adoption requires pilot targets and hard constraints to pass.

openings.claim: Counterfactual: forbid full workshop assembly before packing. Supply the existing base/exterior with loose, complete partitions and an order-specific placement map locating every short partition.
openings.delta: Transfers insertion to customers and replaces the generic diagram with ordered-layout guidance; geometry and removable connections remain.
openings.prediction: Workshop insertion time falls; reaching eight minutes depends on checking/packing overhead. Customer success could improve with the map or worsen with additional assembly.
openings.probe: Separately time selection, insertion, checking and packing for matched assembled and loose-part samples. Ten participants attempt assigned layouts unaided using counterbalanced reusable samples; record placement errors and completion. Inspect loose-part containment and calculate material cost.
assumptions: Replacement dependencies: accurate order-to-parts/map matching; legible cues; counted partition containment; customer ability and willingness to insert partitions; reliable existing slots; sample preparation and printing within budget and deadline.

openings.claim: Counterfactual: forbid shared shape-bin picking during assembly. Stage each order in a reusable board tray marking every required part and exterior color, then assemble from that tray.
openings.delta: Makes selection an explicit order-complete staging step while retaining workshop assembly.
openings.prediction: If selection interference contributes to mixed-layout delays, trays reduce long orders and discrepancies after counting staging labor.
openings.probe: Alternate matched mixed-layout runs between bins and trays; include staging, tray reset and checking in total worker time. Reconcile contents against order slips and count/color requirements. Reject adoption without improved time and completeness.
assumptions: Replacement dependencies: correct component lists and tray markings; explicit order identity; bench space; assigned staging responsibility; independent contents check; reusable trays and reset/storage labor within budget, available working time and delivery limits.

openings.claim: Stage labeled, part/color-marked reusable order trays; retain full assembly.
openings.discriminator: Selection interference versus layout complexity; assembly dominance unproven.
openings.probe: Balance workers/layouts; alternate bins/trays, record transitions; separately time selection/insertion/checking/packing including staging/reset; independently reconcile contents.
openings.uncertainty: Correct lists/markings/identity, responsibility, bench/storage space and total labor remain dependencies.

openings.claim: Order-specific short-partition diagrams may resolve placement ambiguity.
openings.discriminator: Reduced wrong slots/help with unchanged retries distinguishes guidance from insertion difficulty.
openings.probe: Complete kits; balance layouts across five current/five specific-diagram first-use trials; record ten-minute unaided correctness, help, placement errors and retries.
openings.uncertainty: Exploratory; overlapping widths leave mechanical causes unresolved.

openings.claim: Supply existing base/exterior, complete loose partitions and ordered-layout map; transfer insertion to customers.
openings.discriminator: Insertion savings versus checking/packing overhead and customer burden.
openings.probe: Time matched assembled/loose samples by activity; counterbalance reusable customer trials; record errors/completion; inspect containment and cost.
openings.uncertainty: Parts/map matching, legibility, counted containment, reliable slots and customer ability/willingness remain dependencies.

post_distill.decision: Unvalidated; complaints do not establish verified defect rate. Share 15 samples/ten participants across exploratory probes. Preserve 30x20 cm footprint, assortment, removable partitions, accepted counts/colors and delivery; initial cost <=500, added materials <=0.40/order. Adoption requires 60-unit pilot: >=98% complete, median <=8 minutes, >=90% unaided.
